annotatedSteps.description: Convert tan θ and cot θ into sin θ and cos θ
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
LHS = tan θ / (1 − cot θ) + cot θ / (1 − tan θ)
= (sin θ / cos θ) / ((sin θ − cos θ)/sin θ) + (cos θ / sin θ) / ((cos θ − sin θ)/cos θ)
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct conversion into terms of sin θ and cos θ

annotatedSteps.description: Simplify to fractions and combine over a common denominator
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
= sin² θ / (cos θ(sin θ − cos θ)) + cos² θ / (sin θ(sin θ − cos θ))
= (sin³ θ − cos³ θ) / (sin θ cos θ (sin θ − cos θ))
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ½ Sign error in intermediate line: taking out negative sign from (cos θ − sin θ) requires changing '+' to '−'
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking:
= sin² θ / (cos θ(sin θ − cos θ)) − cos² θ / (sin θ(sin θ − cos θ))
= (sin³ θ − cos³ θ) / (sin θ cos θ (sin θ − cos θ))

annotatedSteps.description: Factorize numerator using a³ − b³ and simplify to RHS
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
= (sin θ − cos θ)(sin² θ + sin θ cos θ + cos² θ) / (sin θ cos θ (sin θ − cos θ))
= (1 + sin θ cos θ) / (sin θ cos θ) = 1 + sec θ cosec θ = RHS
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct algebraic expansion, simplification and final identity proven

teacherNote: Well done on structuring the proof and applying the algebraic identity correctly. Be careful with signs: changing (cos θ − sin θ) to (sin θ − cos θ) in the denominator requires changing the '+' between terms to a '−'.

rubric.point: Expressing tan θ and cot θ in terms of sin θ and cos θ and simplifying denominators
Taking LCM and forming (sin³ θ − cos³ θ) / [sin θ cos θ (sin θ − cos θ)] with correct sign
Using identity a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) and simplifying to RHS (1 + sec θ cosec θ)
